item.title: ‘Pueblo Revolt’ opens at Perseverance, and Dr. X̱’unei Lance Twitchell on new MA in Teaching Indigenous Languages at UAS
item.description: Juneau Afternoon featuring Professor X̱’unei Lance Twitchell on the future MA in Teaching Indigenous Languages degree at UAS, and a preview of "Pueblo Revolt" opening at Perseverance Theatre on February 27.

item.title: Q&A with Juneau’s Harbormaster as cleanup continues from intense winter storms
item.description: Ten boats sank in Juneau harbors during the intense winter storms that struck at the beginning of the year. The city is still dealing with the aftermath.

item.title: Alaskans trying to repeal ranked choice voting sue over ballot wording
item.description: A repeal measure will appear on the ballot this year. What it says, exactly, is in dispute.

item.title: Alaska House approves $490M fast-track budget bill, but savings draw in question
item.description: For now, with the failure of a three-quarters vote necessary to access state savings, the bill has no way to pay for the expenses it calls for.

item.title: Army Corps backs out of plan to study lake tap as long-term Mendenhall Valley flood solution
item.description: Juneau’s City Manager Katie Koester shared the news at a Juneau Assembly committee meeting Monday night. She called the Army Corps’ change of position deeply frustrating.

item.title: Department of the Interior set to cede millions of acres of public land to the State of Alaska
item.description: State officials are calling it a win for Alaska's economic sovereignty, but some residents are worried about losing longstanding subsistence rights.

item.title: Juneau School Board selects three finalists for new superintendent
item.description: Two candidates are already based in Juneau, and all three have experience with education in Alaska.

item.title: Survey says streets, schools and safety among Juneau’s top priorities ahead of looming city cuts
item.description: The Juneau Assembly will use the results to figure out how to mend the estimated $10 to $12 million recurring hole in the city’s budget resulting from last fall's ballot initiatives.
